title: Greeting from the Roman church to the Corinthian church
english: The church of God that sojourns in Rome writes to the church of God that sojourns in Corinth, to those who are called and sanctified in the will of God through our Lord Jesus Christ. May grace and peace from almighty God be multiplied to you through Jesus Christ.
orientation: The letter opens with the Roman church's formal greeting to the Corinthian church, invoking grace and peace from God through Jesus Christ.

title: Delayed reply because of disasters; praise of Corinth's former virtue
english: Because sudden and repeated misfortunes and calamities have fallen upon us, we think we have been slow to respond to the matters you have asked about, beloved. We mean that defiled and unholy faction, alien and foreign to the elect of God, which a few rash and arrogant individuals have kindled to such a pitch of folly that your revered name, famous and worthy of love among all people, has been greatly blasphemed.

For who has ever visited you and not approved your all-virtuous and firm faith? Who has not admired your sober and gentle piety in Christ? Who has not proclaimed the magnificent character of your hospitality? Who has not called your perfect and secure knowledge blessed?

For you did everything without partiality and walked in the ordinances of God. You submitted to your leaders and gave due honor to the elders among you. You instructed the young to think moderate and reverent thoughts. You directed the women to accomplish everything with a blameless, reverent, and pure conscience, loving their husbands as is fitting. You taught them to manage their household affairs with reverence, remaining within the proper order of submission, exercising complete self-control.
orientation: The Roman church is writing to the Corinthian church, explaining why their reply has been slow and then praising the Corinthians' former good conduct before rebuking their present faction.

title: The Corinthians' former humility and peace
english: You were all humble-minded, with no trace of boasting. You submitted rather than ruled, and you were happier to give than to receive. You were content with the provisions of Christ, and you had stored his words carefully in your inward parts. His sufferings were before your eyes.
So a deep and rich peace was given to all, and an insatiable desire for doing good, and a full outpouring of the Holy Spirit came upon everyone.
Full of holy counsel, in good eagerness with reverent confidence, you stretched out your hands to God the Almighty, beseeching him to be merciful if you had sinned unwillingly.
It was a contest for you day and night on behalf of the whole brotherhood, so that the number of the elect of God might be saved with mercy and a good conscience.
You were sincere and innocent and without memory of wrongs toward one another.
Every faction and every division was abominable to you. You mourned over the transgressions of your neighbors; you judged their shortcomings to be your own.
You never regretted any act of doing good, ready for every good work.

Adorned with a wholly virtuous and reverent way of life, you accomplished everything in the fear of him. The commandments and the righteous requirements of the Lord were written on the broad places of your hearts.
orientation: The Roman church is recalling the Corinthians' former virtuous conduct before the faction arose.

title: From prosperity to faction: the fall of Corinth
english: You were given every glory and abundance, and what is written was fulfilled: "He ate and drank, and grew large and fat, and the beloved kicked." (Deuteronomy 32:15)
From this came envy and spite, strife and faction, persecution and disorder, war and captivity.
So the dishonored were stirred up against the honored, the inglorious against the glorious, the foolish against the wise, the young against the elders.

For this reason righteousness and peace stand far away. Each one has abandoned the fear of God and become dim-sighted in his faith. Each one no longer walks in the lawful paths of God's commandments or conducts himself as is fitting for Christ. Instead, each one walks according to the desires of his own wicked heart, having taken up unjust and impious envy, through which death entered the world.
orientation: The Roman church is addressing the Corinthians, recalling how their former glory and prosperity fulfilled Scripture, and how envy then produced faction and every evil.

title: Envy from Cain to David
english: For it is written this way: “After some days had passed, Cain brought a sacrifice to God from the fruits of the earth, and Abel also brought one from the firstborn of his sheep and from their fat portions.
God looked with favor on Abel and his gifts, but on Cain and his sacrifices He did not attend.
Cain was grieved exceedingly, and his face fell.
God said to Cain, ‘Why are you so deeply grieved, and why has your face fallen? If you offer rightly but do not divide rightly, have you not sinned?
Be still. His turning is toward you, and you will rule over him.’
Cain said to his brother Abel, ‘Let us go out into the plain.’ And while they were in the plain, Cain rose up against his brother Abel and killed him.”
You see, brothers, envy and spite brought about brother-murder.
Because of envy, our father Jacob fled from the face of his brother Esau.
Envy caused Joseph to be pursued to the point of death and to enter into slavery.

Envy forced Moses to flee from the face of Pharaoh, king of Egypt, when he heard his fellow-tribesman say, “Who appointed you judge or magistrate over us? Do you want to kill me, just as you killed the Egyptian yesterday?”
Because of envy, Aaron and Miriam had to lodge outside the camp.
Envy brought Dathan and Abiram down alive into Hades, because they made faction against Moses, the servant of God.
Because of envy, David incurred envy not only from the foreigners, but he was also pursued by Saul, king of Israel.
orientation: The Roman church has just begun its letter to Corinth and now opens its scriptural argument by showing how envy has worked murder and persecution from the very first brothers onward.

title: From ancient examples to the apostles' contests
english: But let us stop drawing on ancient examples and come to the athletes who lived closest to us. Let us take the noble examples of our own generation.
Because of envy and spite, the greatest and most righteous pillars were persecuted and struggled all the way to death.
Let us set before our eyes the good apostles.
Peter, because of unjust envy, endured not one or two but many hardships, and having borne witness in this way he went to the place of glory that was due him.
Because of envy and strife, Paul showed the prize of endurance.
He wore chains seven times, was exiled, was stoned, became a herald in both the East and the West, and received the noble fame of his faith.

He taught righteousness to the whole world, and when he had reached the boundary of the West and borne witness before the rulers, he was released from the world in this way and was taken up into the holy place, becoming the greatest pattern of endurance.
orientation: The Roman church has just listed ancient examples of envy's harm and now turns to the recent apostles as models of endurance.

title: Envy's victims become examples
english: A great multitude of the elect gathered around these men who had conducted themselves in holiness. Because of envy they suffered many outrages and tortures, and among us they became a most beautiful example.
Because of envy women were persecuted as Danaids and Dircae. They suffered terrible and unholy torments, yet they finished the race of faith, and they who were weak in body received a noble prize.
Envy estranged wives from husbands and changed what our father Adam said: “This now is bone of my bones and flesh of my flesh” (Genesis 2:23).
Envy and faction overthrew great cities and rooted out great nations.
orientation: Clement is piling up examples of the harm envy has done, moving from the apostles to other faithful sufferers and to the destructive power of envy in families and cities.

title: Repentance as the Path Back to God
english: We are writing these things to you, beloved, not only to admonish you but also to remind ourselves. For we are in the same arena, and the same contest lies before us.
So let us abandon empty and vain cares, and let us come to the glorious and venerable rule of our tradition. Let us see what is good and pleasing and acceptable in the sight of the one who made us.
Let us gaze at the blood of Christ and know how precious it is to his Father. It was poured out for our salvation, and it brought the grace of repentance to the whole world.
Let us go through all the generations and learn thoroughly that in generation after generation the Master has given a place of repentance to those who wish to turn back to him.
Noah preached repentance, and those who obeyed were saved.
Jonah preached destruction to the Ninevites. But they repented of their sins, propitiated God by their supplications, and received salvation, even though they were strangers to God.
orientation: The Roman church, writing to the Corinthians, has just shown how envy and faction destroyed great cities and nations, and now turns to exhortation, urging the Corinthians to abandon empty cares and return to the rule of tradition, looking to Christ's blood and the examples of Noah and Jonah as proof that God gives a place of repentance in every generation.

title: God's Oath-Bound Call to Repentance
english: The ministers of God's grace spoke about repentance through the Holy Spirit.
And the Lord of all things himself spoke about repentance with an oath: 'As I live, says the Lord, I do not desire the death of the sinner as much as repentance.' And he added this good counsel:

'Repent, house of Israel, from your lawlessness. I said to the sons of my people: Even if your sins reach from earth to heaven, and even if they are redder than scarlet and blacker than sackcloth, if you turn to me with your whole heart and say, "Father," I will listen to you as to a holy people.'

And in another place he says this: 'Wash and become clean; remove the wickedness from your souls, away from my eyes. Stop your wicked deeds; learn to do good; seek justice; rescue the wronged; give judgment for the orphan and justice for the widow. Come now, and let us reason together, says the Lord. Even if your sins are like crimson, I will make them white as snow; even if they are like scarlet, I will make them white as wool. If you are willing and listen to me, you will eat the good things of the land; but if you are not willing and do not listen to me, a sword will devour you. For the mouth of the Lord has spoken these things.'
So, wanting all his beloved ones to share in repentance, he established them by his all-powerful will.
orientation: The Roman church is citing Scripture to show that God has always offered repentance, now quoting the ministers of grace and the Master himself speaking with an oath.

title: Obey God's will and turn from envy to the examples of Enoch and Noah
english: Therefore let us obey his magnificent and glorious will. Let us fall before him as suppliants of his mercy and goodness, and turn to his compassions. Let us leave behind the vain toil, the strife, and the envy that leads to death.
Let us look intently at those who ministered perfectly to his magnificent glory.
Let us take Enoch. He was found righteous in obedience, and he was translated, and no death of his was found.
Noah was found faithful. Through his ministry he proclaimed a regeneration to the world, and through him the Master saved the living creatures that entered the ark in harmony.
orientation: Clement, writing from the Roman church to the Corinthian church, has just quoted Isaiah's call to repentance and now urges the Corinthians to obey God's will and look to ancient examples of faithful ministry.

title: Abraham's obedience, faith, and hospitality
english: Abraham was called the friend of God, and he was found faithful because he obeyed the words of God.

Through obedience he left his own land, his relatives, and his father's house. He gave up a small land, a weak family, and a little house so that he might inherit the promises of God. For God says to him: "Go from your land and from your relatives and from your father's house to the land that I will show you. I will make you into a great nation, and I will bless you and make your name great, and you will be blessed. I will bless those who bless you and curse those who curse you, and in you all the tribes of the earth will be blessed" (Genesis 12:1-3).

Again, when Abraham was separated from Lot, God said to him: "Lift up your eyes and look from the place where you are now, toward the north and the south and the east and the sea, for all the land that you see I will give to you and to your descendants forever. And I will make your descendants like the sand of the earth; if anyone can count the sand of the earth, then your descendants also will be counted" (Genesis 13:14-16).

And again Scripture says: "God brought Abraham out and said to him: 'Look up to heaven and count the stars, if you are able to count them. So shall your descendants be.' And Abraham believed God, and it was reckoned to him for righteousness" (Genesis 15:5-6).
Because of faith and hospitality a son was given to him in old age, and through obedience he offered him as a sacrifice to God at the mountain which God showed him.
orientation: The Roman church continues its list of ancient examples of obedience, now turning to Abraham, whom God called out of his homeland and blessed with promises.

title: Lot saved, his wife made a sign
english: Because of his hospitality and piety, Lot was saved from Sodom when the whole surrounding region was judged with fire and brimstone. The Lord made it clear that he does not abandon those who hope in him, but hands over to punishment and torment those who lean another way.

For when his wife went out with him, she was of a different mind and not in harmony. She was made a sign of this: she became a pillar of salt and remains so to this day. This was so that everyone would know that the double-minded and those who doubt the power of God become a judgment and a warning to all generations.
orientation: Clement is giving examples from Scripture of how faith, hospitality, and obedience bring salvation while envy and double-mindedness bring judgment, now turning to Lot and his wife.

title: Rahab saved by faith and hospitality
english: Rahab the prostitute was saved because of her faith and hospitality.

Joshua son of Nun sent spies into Jericho. The king of the land learned that they had come to spy out his country, so he sent men to seize them, intending to put them to death once they were captured.
But the hospitable Rahab took the spies in and hid them in the upper room under the flax stalks.

When the king's men arrived, they said, 'The spies of our land have come to you. Bring them out, for the king commands it.' She answered, 'The men you are looking for did come to me, but they left at once and are on their way,' while pointing them in the opposite direction.

Then she said to the spies, 'I know for certain that the Lord God is giving you this land, for fear and trembling of you has fallen on all who live in it. So when you take it, save me and my father's household.'
They said to her, 'It will be as you have said. When you learn that we are coming, gather all your people under your roof, and they will be saved. For whoever is found outside the house will perish.'

They also gave her a sign, so that she would hang a scarlet cord from her house. This made it clear in advance that through the blood of the Lord there will be redemption for all who believe and hope in God.
You see, beloved, that not only faith but also prophecy was at work in this woman.
orientation: Clement is giving examples from Scripture of faith and hospitality, and has just begun the story of Rahab the prostitute in Jericho.

title: Call to humility and the Lord's commands
english: So then, brothers and sisters, let us be humble-minded. Let us put away all arrogance, conceit, folly, and anger, and let us do what is written. For the Holy Spirit says: “Let not the wise boast in their wisdom, nor the strong in their strength, nor the rich in their riches; but let the one who boasts boast in the Lord, seeking him and doing justice and righteousness” (Jeremiah 9:23-24). Above all, let us remember the words of the Lord Jesus, which he spoke when he taught gentleness and patience.

For he said: “Show mercy, so that you may receive mercy. Forgive, so that you may be forgiven. As you do, so it will be done to you. As you give, so it will be given to you. As you judge, so you will be judged. As you show kindness, so kindness will be shown to you. With the measure you use, it will be measured back to you.”

With this command and these instructions let us steady ourselves, so that we walk in obedience to his holy words, humble-minded. For the holy word says: “On whom will I look, but on the one who is gentle and quiet and trembles at my words?” (Isaiah 66:2).
orientation: The Roman church is addressing the Corinthians, urging them to abandon arrogance and obey the Lord's words on mercy and humility.

title: Obey God rather than leaders of envy
english: So it is right and holy, men who are brothers, for us to obey God rather than follow the leaders of hateful envy in their arrogance and disorder.

For we will suffer no ordinary harm. On the contrary, we will face great danger if we recklessly hand ourselves over to the wishes of people who drive us into strife and factions to estrange us from what is good. Let us be kind to one another, in keeping with the compassion and gentleness of the one who made us.

For it is written: "The upright will dwell in the land, and the innocent will be left in it, but the lawless will be destroyed from it" (Proverbs 2:21-22). And again Scripture says: "I saw the wicked exalted and lifted high like the cedars of Lebanon, and I passed by, and behold, he was gone, and I sought his place and did not find it. Keep innocence and look to uprightness, for there is a remnant for a peaceable man" (Psalm 37:35-37).
orientation: The writer from Rome urges the Corinthians to obey God rather than follow the few who stir envy and faction against the elders.

title: Cling to the Sincere Peacemakers, Not the Hypocrites
english: So let us cling to those who make peace with piety, and not to those who only wish for peace with hypocrisy.
For he says somewhere: “This people honors me with their lips, but their heart is far distant from me” (Isaiah 29:13).
And again: “With their mouth they blessed, but with their heart they cursed” (Psalm 62:4).
And again he says: “They loved him with their mouth and lied to him with their tongue, but their heart was not upright with him, nor were they faithful in his covenant” (Psalm 78:36 LXX).

For this reason let the deceitful lips that speak lawlessness against the righteous become speechless. And again: “May the Lord destroy all the deceitful lips, the boastful tongue, those who said: ‘We will magnify our tongue; our lips are our own; who is lord over us?’” (Psalm 12:3-4).
“Because of the misery of the poor and the groaning of the needy, now I will arise,” says the Lord; “I will place him in safety; I will speak boldly in him” (Psalm 12:5).
orientation: Clement, writing from the Roman church to the Corinthian church, is urging the Corinthians to separate themselves from the faction and to join those who pursue peace sincerely, supporting this with scriptural quotations about hypocritical lips and hearts.

title: The humble Christ as our pattern
english: Christ belongs to those who have humility, not to those who exalt themselves over his flock. The sceptre of the greatness of God, the Lord Jesus Christ, did not come with boastful arrogance or pride, though he could have done so. He came having humility, just as the Holy Spirit spoke about him. For this is what the Spirit says.

"Lord, who has believed our report, and to whom has the arm of the Lord been revealed? We proclaimed before him as a child, as a root in thirsty ground. He has no form or glory, and we saw him, and he had no form or beauty. His form was dishonored, fading beside the form of men. He was a man under blows and toil, knowing how to bear weakness, for his face was turned away. He was dishonored and not esteemed. He bears our sins and suffers for us, yet we thought he was under toil and blows and affliction. But he was wounded for our sins and weakened for our lawless deeds. The discipline of our peace is upon him, and by his bruise we were healed. We all went astray like sheep, each one straying on his own way, and the Lord handed him over for our sins. Because he was afflicted, he does not open his mouth. He was led like a sheep to slaughter, and like a lamb silent before its shearer, so he does not open his mouth. In his humiliation his judgment was taken away. Who will tell of his generation? For his life is taken from the earth. He goes to death for the lawless deeds of my people. And I will give the wicked for his burial and the rich for his death, for he did no lawlessness, and no deceit was found in his mouth. The Lord desires to cleanse him from the blow. If you make an offering for sin, your soul will see long-lived offspring. The Lord desires to lift the toil from his soul, to show him light and to shape him with understanding, to justify a righteous one who serves many well, and he himself will bear their sins. Therefore he will inherit many and will divide spoil with the strong, because his soul was handed over to death and he was counted among the lawless. He bore the sins of many and was handed over for their sins." (Isaiah 53:1-12)

"And again he himself says: 'But I am a worm and not a man, a reproach of men and contempt of the people. All who saw me mocked me, spoke with their lips, and shook their heads. He trusted in the Lord, let him rescue him, let him save him, since he delights in him.'" (Psalm 22:6-8)
See, dear friends, what pattern was given to us. If the Lord had humility in this way, what are we to do, we who have come through him under the yoke of his grace?
orientation: The author presents Christ as the example of humility against the envy and faction in Corinth, quoting what the Holy Spirit said about him.

title: Imitators of the humble prophets
english: Let us also imitate those who walked about in goatskins and sheepskins, proclaiming the coming of Christ. We mean the prophets Elijah, Elisha, and Ezekiel, and in addition to these, the ones who have been attested.
Abraham was greatly attested and was called a friend of God. Gazing into the glory of God, he humbles himself and says, “But I am earth and ashes” (Genesis 18:27).
And concerning Job it is written in this way: “Job was righteous and blameless, truthful, godly, keeping away from every evil” (Job 1:1).
But Job accuses himself, saying, “No one is clean from filth, not even if his life lasts a single day” (Job 14:4 LXX).

Moses was called faithful in his whole house (Numbers 12:7), and through his ministry God judged Egypt through the plagues and torments upon them. But even Moses, though greatly glorified, did not boast greatly. Instead, when an oracle was given to him from the bush, he said, “Who am I, that you send me? But I am slow of speech and tongue” (Exodus 3:11; 4:10).
And again Moses says, “But I am like vapor from a pot.”
orientation: Clement is urging the Corinthians to imitate the humility of the prophets and patriarchs, after showing that Christ himself humbled himself.

title: David's confession of sin and plea for cleansing
english: What then should we say about David, who was testified about? God said of him: “I found a man after my heart, David the son of Jesse; in eternal mercy I anointed him.”
But David himself says to God: “Have mercy on me, O God, according to your great mercy, and according to the abundance of your compassion blot out my transgression.
Wash me thoroughly from my lawlessness, and cleanse me from my sin. For I know my transgression, and my sin is always before me.
Against you alone have I sinned, and I have done what is evil in your sight, so that you may be justified in your words and prevail when you are judged.
For behold, I was conceived in transgressions, and in sins my mother conceived me.
For behold, you have loved truth; the hidden and secret things of your wisdom you have made clear to me.
You will sprinkle me with hyssop, and I will be clean; you will wash me, and I will be whiter than snow.
You will make me hear joy and gladness; the bones that have been humbled will rejoice.
Turn your face away from my sins, and blot out all my transgressions.
Create in me a clean heart, O God, and renew a right spirit within my inward parts.
Do not cast me away from your face, and do not take your Holy Spirit from me.
Restore to me the joy of your salvation, and steady me with a guiding spirit.
I will teach the lawless your ways, and the ungodly will turn back to you.
Deliver me from bloodshed, O God, the God of my salvation.
My tongue will rejoice in your righteousness. Lord, you will open my mouth, and my lips will declare your praise.
For if you had wanted sacrifice, I would have given it; you take no pleasure in whole burnt offerings.
The sacrifice to God is a broken spirit; a broken and humbled heart God will not despise.”
orientation: Clement has been citing examples of humble self-accusation from Scripture, and now turns to David, whom God himself testified about, quoting David's own words of repentance from Psalm 50 (LXX).

title: The Humility of the Ancients and the Peace of God
english: So many examples, and such great ones, have been attested in this way. Through obedience, humility and lowliness have made better not only us, but also the generations before us, those who received God's oracles in fear and truth.

Since we have shared in many great and glorious deeds, let us run back to the goal of peace that was handed down to us from the beginning. Let us gaze upon the Father and Creator of the whole world, and let us cling to his magnificent and surpassing gifts of peace and his acts of kindness.
Let us see him with our understanding, and let us look with the eyes of the soul at his patient will. Let us consider how free from anger he is toward all his creation.
orientation: Clement has just quoted Psalm 51 at length, and now he turns from the example of David's repentance to the general lesson that humility and obedience have made past generations better, and he calls the Corinthians to return to the goal of peace and to contemplate God's patient will.

title: The ordered peace of creation
english: The heavens move at his direction and submit to him in peace.
Day and night complete the course he has set for them, and neither hinders the other.
Sun and moon and the choirs of stars roll through the boundaries he has assigned them in harmony, without any deviation.

The earth conceives according to his will and in its own seasons brings forth food for the teeming multitude of humans and beasts and all the living creatures on it. It does not dissent from anything he has decreed, nor alter it.
The unsearchable depths of the abysses and the indescribable regions of the underworld are held together by the same commands.
The vast expanse of the boundless sea was gathered together by his creative work into its reservoirs. It does not transgress the bars placed around it, but does just as he commanded it.
For he said, “Thus far shall you come, and your waves shall be broken within you” (Job 38:11).
The ocean, impassable to humans, and the worlds beyond it are directed by the same ordinances of the Master.
Spring and summer and autumn and winter pass into one another in peace.
The stations of the winds perform their ministry at their proper time without stumbling.
The ever-flowing springs, created for enjoyment and health, offer their breasts for human life without fail.
Even the smallest of living creatures make their gatherings in harmony and peace.

All these things the great Creator and Master of all things commanded to exist in peace and harmony. He does good to all things, and superabundantly to us who have fled for refuge to his mercies through our Lord Jesus Christ,
to whom be glory and majesty forever and ever. Amen.
orientation: The Roman church is describing how all parts of creation obey God's ordered will in peace and harmony, as a model for the Corinthians.

title: Live worthily before the all-seeing God
english: Take care, beloved, that God's many benefits do not become judgment for us. This will happen if we fail to live worthily of him and to do what is good and pleasing in his sight with harmony.
For he says somewhere: "The spirit of the Lord is a lamp searching the inner chambers of the belly" (Proverbs 20:27).
Let us consider how near he is, and that none of our thoughts or the reasonings we make escapes his notice.
It is right, then, that we should not desert his will.
Let us offend foolish and thoughtless people, people who exalt themselves and boast in the arrogance of their words, rather than God.

Let us reverence the Lord Jesus Christ, whose blood was given for us. Let us respect our leaders. Let us honor the elders. Let us train the young in the discipline of the fear of God. Let us guide our wives toward what is good.

Let them display the lovable character of purity. Let them demonstrate the sincere will of their gentleness. Let them make the moderation of their tongue evident through silence. Let them offer their love not according to partialities, but equally to all who fear God in holiness.

Let our children share in the discipline that is in Christ. Let them learn how much humility prevails with God, how much pure love can accomplish with God, how the fear of him is good and great and saves all who conduct themselves in it in holiness with a pure mind.
For he is the searcher of thoughts and reflections. His breath is in us, and when he wills, he will take it away.
orientation: The Roman church, having just praised God's ordered creation, now turns to exhort the Corinthians directly about their conduct before God.

title: Faith in Christ confirms all these commands
english: Faith in Christ confirms all these things. For Christ himself calls us through the Holy Spirit, and this is what he says:

“Come, children, listen to me; I will teach you the fear of the Lord. Who is the person who desires life, who loves to see good days? Stop your tongue from evil, and your lips from speaking deceit. Turn away from evil, and do good. Seek peace, and pursue it. The eyes of the Lord are on the righteous, and his ears are open to their supplication; but the face of the Lord is against those who do evil, to destroy utterly the memory of them from the earth. The righteous one cried out, and the Lord heard him, and rescued him from all his afflictions. Many are the scourges of the sinner, but mercy will surround those who hope in the Lord” (Psalm 34:11-17; Psalm 32:10).
orientation: Clement has just finished a long series of moral exhortations to wives, children, and all who fear God, and now grounds them in the call of Christ through the Holy Spirit, quoting Psalm 33 (LXX) as the voice of Christ.

title: The double-minded must not doubt God's swift gifts
english: The Father is compassionate in every way and rich in good works. He feels tenderly toward those who fear him, and he gently and kindly gives his gifts to those who come to him with a sincere mind.
So let us not be double-minded, and let us not let our souls be deceived by his surpassing and glorious gifts.

Let this Scripture be far from us, where it says: “Wretched are the double-minded, those who doubt in their soul, those who say: ‘We heard these things even in the days of our fathers, and look, we have grown old, and none of these things has happened to us.’”

You fools, compare yourselves to a tree. Take a vine: first it sheds its leaves, then a shoot comes, then a leaf, then a flower, and after these a sour grape, then a ripe grape standing ready. You see that in a short time the fruit of the tree reaches ripeness.

Truly his will will be brought to completion quickly and suddenly, as Scripture also bears witness, that he will come quickly and will not delay, and the Lord will come suddenly to his temple, and the Holy One whom you expect will come.
orientation: The Roman church continues its appeal, now warning the Corinthians against doubting God's promised gifts by quoting a now-lost scripture about the double-minded and the vine's swift fruit.

title: Nature's daily and yearly resurrections foreshadow the future resurrection
english: Let us consider, beloved, how the Master continually shows us that the resurrection is about to be. He made the Lord Jesus Christ its firstfruits by raising him from the dead.
Let us look, beloved, at the resurrection that happens in its season.
Day and night show us a resurrection. Night sleeps, and day rises. Day departs, and night comes on.
Let us take the fruits. How does the seed come about, and in what manner?

The sower went out and cast each of the seeds into the ground. They fall into the ground dry and bare, and they dissolve. Then from their dissolution the majesty of the Master's providence raises them up, and from the one seed he increases more and brings forth fruit.
orientation: The Roman church, addressing the Corinthians as 'beloved,' is beginning a series of examples from the natural world to show that God constantly demonstrates the future resurrection.

title: The Phoenix as a Sign of Resurrection
english: Let us consider the strange sign that takes place in the eastern regions, that is, in the parts around Arabia.

There is a bird there called the phoenix. It is the only one of its kind, and it lives five hundred years. When the time of its death has drawn near, it makes for itself a nest of frankincense, myrrh, and the remaining spices. When the time is fulfilled, it enters the nest and dies.

As the flesh decays, a worm is born. Nourished by the moisture of the dead creature, the worm grows wings. Then, when it has become strong, it takes up that nest where the bones of the former bird are. Carrying them, it travels from the land of Arabia to Egypt, to the city called Heliopolis.
In daylight, while all watch, it flies to the altar of the sun and places them there. Then it turns back.
The priests then examine the records of the times and find that it has come when the five hundredth year has been completed.
orientation: Clement is giving examples from nature that point to resurrection, and now turns to the story of the phoenix in Arabia.

title: Resurrection promised through the phoenix and Scripture
english: Should we then consider it a great and wonderful thing that the creator of all things will raise up those who have served him in holiness, with confidence in good faith? After all, he shows us the majesty of his promise even through a bird.
For he says somewhere: “You will raise me up, and I will confess to you,” and: “I lay down and slept; I woke again, because you are with me” (Psalm 3:5).
And again Job says: “And you will raise up this flesh of mine, which has drained all these things” (Job 19:26).
orientation: The Roman church is arguing that God will raise the dead, using the phoenix as a natural sign and then quoting Scripture.

title: God's power and truthfulness ground our hope
english: So let our souls be bound to this hope, to the one who is faithful in his promises and just in his judgments.
The one who commanded us not to lie will certainly not lie himself. For nothing is impossible with God except lying.
So let his faith be rekindled in us, and let us understand that all things are near to him.
By the word of his majesty he established all things, and by a word he can destroy them.

Who will say to him, “What have you done?” Or who will stand against the might of his strength? He will do all things when he wills and as he wills, and none of the things decreed by him will pass away.
All things are before him, and nothing has escaped his counsel.

The heavens declare the glory of God, and the firmament proclaims the work of his hands. Day pours forth speech to day, and night announces knowledge to night. There are no words or speeches whose voices are not heard (Psalm 19:1-4).
orientation: The author has just cited Scripture about resurrection and now turns to God's faithfulness and power as the ground for hope.

title: No Escape from the All-Encompassing God
english: Since everything is seen and everything is heard, let us fear him. Let us abandon the defiled desires of evil works, so that his mercy may shelter us from the judgments that are about to come.
Where can any of us flee from his mighty hand? What world will take in anyone who deserts him?

The writing says somewhere: Where can I go, and where can I hide from your face? If I climb up into heaven, you are there. If I travel to the ends of the earth, your right hand is there. If I spread out into the depths, your spirit is there (Psalm 139:7-8).
So where can anyone go, or where can he escape, from the one who encompasses all things?
orientation: The Roman church, having just quoted Psalm 19 on God's all-seeing knowledge, now urges the Corinthians to fear God and abandon evil desires, since no one can flee from his mighty hand.

title: Approach God in holiness as his chosen portion
english: Let us approach him, then, in holiness of soul, lifting pure and undefiled hands toward him, and loving our gentle and compassionate Father, who made us a portion of choice for himself.

For it is written this way: When the Most High was dividing the nations, when he scattered the sons of Adam, he set the boundaries of the nations according to the number of God's angels. The Lord's portion became his people Jacob; Israel became the measured line of his inheritance (Deuteronomy 32:8-9).

And in another place he says: Look, the Lord takes for himself a nation from the midst of nations, just as a person takes his firstfruits from the threshing floor; and from that nation will come forth holy things of holies.
orientation: The Roman church is exhorting the Corinthians to draw near to God in holiness, now grounding the call in Scripture about God choosing a people for himself.

title: Holiness, humility, and the praise that comes from God
english: Since we are the portion of the Holy One, then, let us do everything that belongs to holiness. Let us flee slander, defiled and impure entanglements, drunkenness, innovations, and abominable desires, loathsome adultery, and abominable arrogance.
For God, he says, opposes the arrogant, but gives grace to the humble (Proverbs 3:34).

Let us therefore cling to those to whom grace from God has been given. Let us clothe ourselves with harmony, being humble and self-controlled, keeping ourselves far from every whispering and slander, being justified by deeds and not by words.
For he says: The one who speaks much will also hear in return. Or does the fluent speaker think he is righteous? Blessed is the short-lived one born of a woman. Do not become abundant in words.
Let our praise be in God and not from ourselves, for God hates self-praisers. Let the testimony of our good action be given by others, just as it was given to our righteous fathers.
Boldness, self-will, and recklessness belong to those cursed by God; gentleness, humility, and meekness belong to those blessed by God.
orientation: The Roman church continues its moral exhortation to the Corinthians, now urging them to live as God's holy portion by fleeing vices and pursuing humility, since God opposes the proud and gives grace to the humble.

title: The Blessing of the Patriarchs
english: So let us cling to his blessing and consider what the roads of blessing are. Let us unroll the things that happened from the beginning.
Why was our father Abraham blessed? Was it not because he did righteousness and truth through faith?
Isaac knew with confidence what was to come, and he gladly let himself be brought as a sacrifice.
Jacob departed from his own land with humility because of his brother, went to Laban and served him, and the sovereignty over the twelve tribes of Israel was given to him.
orientation: The Roman church is urging the Corinthians to cling to God's blessing by examining how the patriarchs were blessed through faith, confidence, and humility.

title: All gifts and justification come from God's will, not from ourselves
english: If anyone considers each of these things with a sincere mind, he will recognize the greatness of the gifts given by him.

For from Jacob came the priests and all the Levites who minister at the altar of God. From him came the Lord Jesus according to the flesh. From him came kings and rulers and leaders in the line of Judah, and the rest of his scepters are in no small glory, because God promised, “Your descendants will be like the stars of the sky” (Genesis 22:17).
All of them, then, were glorified and magnified not through themselves or their works or the righteous deeds they accomplished, but through God’s will.

So we too, called through God’s will in Christ Jesus, are not justified through ourselves, nor through our own wisdom or understanding or piety or works done in holiness of heart, but through faith, by which almighty God has justified all those from eternity. To him be glory forever and ever. Amen.
orientation: The Roman church is writing to the Corinthian church, and here it is concluding its long survey of God's blessings from Abraham through Jacob by drawing the lesson that every gift and every justification comes from God's will alone.

title: Doing good works eagerly, since God rejoices in his works
english: What then should we do, brothers? Should we stop doing good and abandon love? May the Master never allow this to happen among us. Instead, let us hasten with earnestness and eagerness to complete every good work.
For the Creator and Master of all things rejoices in his works.

By his all-greatest power he fixed the heavens, and by his incomprehensible understanding he ordered them. He separated the earth from the water surrounding it and set it on the secure foundation of his own will. The living creatures that move upon it he commanded to exist by his own arrangement. The sea and the creatures in it he prepared beforehand and enclosed by his own power.
Above all, he formed with his holy and blameless hands man, most excellent and vast in mind, as the imprint of his own image.
For God says this: “Let us make man according to our image and likeness.” And God made man; male and female he made them (Genesis 1:26-27).
When he had completed all these things, he praised them and blessed them and said, “Increase and multiply” (Genesis 1:28).
Let us see that all the righteous were adorned with good works, and the Lord himself, adorning himself with good works, rejoiced.
Since we have this pattern, let us approach his will without shrinking. With all our strength let us work the work of righteousness.
orientation: The Roman church, having shown that justification comes through faith and God's will, now urges the Corinthians not to slacken from doing good but to imitate God the Creator, who rejoiced in his own good works.

title: The good worker and the reward for good work
english: The good worker receives the bread his work has earned with confidence. The lazy and slack worker cannot face the one who gives him work. So we must be eager for the doing of good, for all things come from him.

For he tells us beforehand, "See the Lord, and his reward is before him, to repay each one according to his work" (Isaiah 40:10). So he urges us, since we believe in him with our whole heart, not to grow idle or slack in any good work.

Let our boast and our confidence be in him. Let us be in submission to his will. Let us consider the whole host of his angels, how they stand beside him and do ministry to his will. For Scripture says, "Ten thousand times ten thousand stood beside him, and a thousand thousands did ministry to him" (Daniel 7:10), and they cried out, "Holy, holy, holy is the Lord of hosts; the whole creation is full of his glory" (Isaiah 6:3).

So we too should gather together in harmony with one conscience and cry to him earnestly as with one voice, so we may become sharers in his great and glorious promises. For Scripture says, "Eye has not seen, and ear has not heard, and it has not entered the human heart, what the Lord has prepared for those who wait for him" (1 Corinthians 2:9).
orientation: The author urges the Corinthians to be eager for good work and to submit to the will of God, holding up the angels as the pattern.

title: The Gifts of God and the Way to Receive Them
english: How blessed and wonderful, beloved, are the gifts of God! Life in immortality, splendor in righteousness, truth with boldness, faith with confidence, self-control with holiness: all these already lie within our understanding. What, then, is being prepared for those who endure? The all-holy Creator and Father of the ages himself knows how great and how beautiful those things are. So let us strive to be found among those who endure, that we may share in the gifts he has promised.

And how shall this be, beloved? It will be if our mind is set faithfully on God; if we seek what pleases him and what he accepts; if we carry out what fits his blameless will and follow the way of truth, casting away from us all wrongdoing and wickedness, greed, quarrels, malice and deceit, gossip and slander, hatred of God, pride and boasting, empty glory and want of hospitality. For those who do these things are hateful to God, and not only those who do them, but those who approve of them as well.

For the Scripture says: “But to the sinner God said: ‘What right have you to recite my statutes, or to take my covenant on your lips? You hated instruction and threw my words behind you. When you saw a thief, you ran along with him, and you threw in your lot with adulterers. Your mouth overflowed with evil, and your tongue wove deceit. You sat and slandered your brother, and laid a stumbling block before your own mother's son. You did these things, and I kept silent; you thought, lawless one, that I would be like you. I will rebuke you and set you before your own face. Consider this, you who forget God, lest he seize you like a lion, with no one to rescue you. A sacrifice of praise will glorify me, and there is the way by which I will show him the salvation of God’” (Psalm 50:16-23).
orientation: Clement, writing from the Roman church to the Corinthian church, has just quoted Scripture about the glory of God's promises and now describes the gifts God has prepared for those who endure.

title: Christ the Way to the Father's Glory
english: This is the way, beloved, in which we found our salvation: Jesus Christ, the high priest of our offerings, the protector and helper of our weakness.

Through him we gaze into the heights of the heavens. Through him we see mirrored his spotless and most exalted face. Through him the eyes of our heart were opened. Through him our foolish and darkened understanding blossoms into the light. Through him the Master willed that we taste immortal knowledge. He is the radiance of his majesty, and he is as much greater than the angels as the name he has inherited is more excellent.
For it is written this way: “He makes his angels spirits, and his ministers a flame of fire” (Psalm 104:4).

But about his Son the Master said this: “You are my Son; today I have begotten you. Ask of me, and I will give you the nations as your inheritance, and the ends of the earth as your possession” (Psalm 2:7-8).
And again he says to him: “Sit at my right hand until I make your enemies a footstool for your feet” (Psalm 110:1).
Who then are the enemies? Those who are wicked and oppose his will.
orientation: The Roman church is addressing the Corinthians, explaining that Jesus Christ is the way through whom they found salvation and through whom God has opened their hearts to light and knowledge.

title: The army and the body as models of ordered submission
english: So then, brothers, let us serve as soldiers with all earnestness in His blameless commandments.
Consider the soldiers who serve under our commanders. Notice how orderly they are, how skillfully they carry out their orders, how submissively they obey.
Not all of them are prefects or tribunes or centurions or commanders of fifty, and so on down the line. But each one, in his own rank, carries out what the king and the commanders order.
The great cannot exist without the small, nor the small without the great. There is a certain blending in all things, and in this blending there is purpose.

Take our own body. The head without the feet is nothing, and the feet without the head are nothing either. The smallest members of our body are necessary and useful to the whole body. All of them breathe together and submit to one rule, so that the whole body may be preserved.
orientation: Clement, writing from the Roman church to the Corinthian church, is urging the Corinthians to abandon their faction by showing how all ordered communities—an army and the human body—work together under one rule.

title: Mutual care and gratitude in the body
english: So let our whole body be kept safe in Christ Jesus, and let each person submit to his neighbor, just as each was placed in the gift God gave him.

Let the strong care for the weak, and let the weak respect the strong. Let the rich supply the poor, and let the poor give thanks to God, because God gave him the means by which his lack might be filled. Let the wise show his wisdom not in words but in good works. Let the one who is humble not testify about himself, but let him allow another to testify about him. Let the one who is pure in the flesh not boast, knowing that another is the one who supplies him with self-control.

Let us consider, then, brothers, from what material we were made, what kind of persons we were when we entered the world, from what tomb and darkness the one who formed and created us brought us into his world, having prepared his benefits before we were born.
Since we have all these things from him, we ought to give thanks to him in everything. To him be glory forever and ever. Amen.
orientation: Clement is applying the image of the body to the Corinthian church, urging each member to act within their God-given gift and to care for one another.

title: Fools mock, but mortals are nothing before God
english: Foolish, senseless, stupid, untaught people mock us and sneer at us, wanting to exalt themselves in their own minds.
For what can a mortal do? Or what strength does an earth-born person have?
For it is written: “There was no form before my eyes, but I heard a breeze and a voice:
What then? Will a mortal be pure before the Lord? Or will a man be blameless in his works, if God does not trust His own servants and perceives something crooked even in His angels?

Heaven itself is not pure in His sight. How much less those who live in houses of clay, since we ourselves are made from that same clay! He struck them as a moth does, and from morning until evening they are no more. Because they could not help themselves, they perished.
He breathed on them, and they died, because they had no wisdom.
But call out, if anyone will answer you, or if you will see any of the holy angels. For anger destroys the fool, and envy kills the one who has gone astray.
I have seen fools putting down roots, but immediately their way of life was devoured.

May their sons be far from salvation. May they be crushed at the doors of their inferiors, and may there be no one to rescue them. For what has been prepared for them, the righteous will eat, but they themselves will not be rescued from evils.”
orientation: Clement has just urged humility and thanksgiving to God; now he quotes Scripture to show that foolish, untaught people mock the faithful, while no mortal is clean or strong before God.

title: Ordered worship at appointed times
english: Since these things are clear to us, and we have looked deeply into the knowledge of God, we must do everything in order, whatever the Lord commanded us to carry out at appointed times.
He commanded that the offerings and ministries be carried out, and not at random or in disorder, but at fixed times and hours.
Where and through whom he wishes them to be carried out, he himself determined by his supreme will, so that everything done in holiness would be acceptable to his will and pleasing to him.
Those who make their offerings at the commanded times are therefore acceptable and blessed, for they follow the Lord's lawful commands and do not go astray.

For to the high priest his own ministries have been given, and to the priests their own place has been assigned, and to the Levites their own services are laid upon them. The lay person is bound by the commands for the laity.
orientation: The Roman church is explaining that God has fixed the times, places, and persons for worship, and that the Corinthians must follow this order.

title: Each in one's own order, with a warning about Jerusalem's exclusive sacrifices
english: Each of us, brothers and sisters, should give thanks to God in his own order, living with a good conscience and not stepping outside the fixed rule of his ministry, in reverence.

Not everywhere, brothers and sisters, are sacrifices of continual offering or of vows or for sin and trespass offered, but only in Jerusalem. And even there they are not offered in every place, but before the temple at the altar, after the thing being offered has been inspected for blemish by the high priest and the ministers mentioned before.
Those, then, who do anything contrary to what is proper to his will have death as the penalty.
You see, brothers and sisters: by as much as we have been deemed worthy of greater knowledge, by so much more are we subject to danger.
orientation: Clement is addressing the Corinthian church directly, applying the previous section's teaching about ordered ministry to each believer and warning that greater knowledge brings greater danger.

title: The apostles' ordered mission from God through Christ
english: The apostles received the good news for us from the Lord Jesus Christ. Jesus the Christ was sent out from God.
So Christ came from God, and the apostles came from Christ. Both things happened in an orderly way, according to God's will.

After they received their commands and were fully assured through the resurrection of our Lord Jesus Christ, and after they were made faithful in the word of God, they went out with the full assurance of the Holy Spirit, proclaiming the good news that the kingdom of God was about to come.
As they preached through the regions and cities, they tested their firstfruits by the Spirit and appointed them as bishops and deacons for those who were about to believe.
This was not a new practice. Long ago it had been written about bishops and deacons, for the scripture says somewhere: "I will appoint their bishops in righteousness and their deacons in faith."
orientation: The author is arguing that God has established a fixed order of ministry, and now traces that order from God through Christ to the apostles and their appointed leaders.

title: Aaron's rod proves God's chosen priesthood
english: And why should it surprise us that those whom God entrusted in Christ with such a work appointed the men we have already mentioned? Even the blessed servant Moses, who was faithful in all God's house, recorded in the sacred books everything that had been commanded to him. The rest of the prophets followed after him, and together they bore witness to the laws he had laid down.

For when envy fell upon the priesthood and the tribes were divided by faction over which of them would be adorned with the glorious name, Moses commanded the twelve tribal chiefs to bring him rods, each inscribed with the name of its tribe. He took the rods, bound them, sealed them with the rings of the tribal chiefs, and placed them in the tent of testimony on the table of God.

Then he closed the tent and sealed the keys just as he had sealed the rods. And he said to them: "Brothers, whichever tribe's rod sprouts, that is the tribe God has chosen to serve as priest and to perform ministry to him."

When morning came, he called together all Israel, the six hundred thousand men, and showed the tribal chiefs the seals. He opened the tent of testimony and brought out the rods. Aaron's rod was found not only to have sprouted but also to be bearing fruit.

What do you think, beloved? Did Moses not know beforehand that this was going to happen? Of course he knew. But he did it this way so that no disorder would arise in Israel, and so that the name of the true and only God would be glorified. To him be glory forever and ever. Amen.
orientation: Clement is arguing that God's appointed order of ministry is ancient and divinely confirmed, and he now turns to Moses and the miracle of Aaron's budding rod as proof.

title: Do not cast out blameless leaders
english: Our apostles knew through our Lord Jesus Christ that strife would arise over the name of the bishop's office. For that reason they acted with complete foreknowledge: they appointed the men already described, and then left further instruction that, if those men fell asleep, other tested men should succeed to their ministry.

Those men were appointed either by the apostles or afterward by other reputable men, with the whole church consenting. They have served Christ's flock blamelessly, with humility, quietly and without baseness, and all have spoken well of them for many years. We do not consider it right to cast such men out from the ministry. For it will be no small sin for us if we cast out those who have offered the gifts of the bishop's office blamelessly and holily.

Blessed are the elders who have gone on ahead, whose departure was fruitful and complete. They do not fear that anyone will move them from the place secured for them. But we see that you have moved some who lived honorably from the ministry that had been blamelessly honored for them.
orientation: The writer from Rome argues that the apostles foresaw disputes over office and provided for approved successors, so removing blameless leaders is unjust.

title: The Scriptures show that the righteous suffer only from the lawless, not from the holy
english: Brothers, you love to contend, and you are zealous for the things that belong to salvation.
You have looked into the sacred Scriptures, the true Scriptures, the ones given through the Holy Spirit.
You know that nothing unjust or falsified has been written in them. You will not find righteous people rejected by holy men.
Righteous people were persecuted, but by lawless men. They were imprisoned, but by unholy men. They were stoned by lawbreakers. They were killed by those who had taken up defiling and unjust envy.
They endured these sufferings gloriously.
What shall we say then, brothers? Was Daniel thrown into the lions' den by those who feared God?

Or were Ananias, Azarias, and Misael shut into the furnace of fire by those who practiced the magnificent and glorious worship of the Most High? May this never happen. Who then were the ones who did these things? The hateful ones, full of every evil, reached such a pitch of rage that they subjected to torment those who were serving God in holy and blameless purpose. They did not know that the Most High is the champion and defender of those who serve His all-virtuous name with a pure conscience. To Him be glory forever and ever. Amen.
But those who endured in confidence inherited glory and honor, and they were lifted up and inscribed by God in His remembrance forever and ever. Amen.
orientation: Clement, writing from the Roman church to the Corinthian church, is rebuking the Corinthians for their faction and now turns to the Scriptures to show that the righteous are never cast out by holy men, but only by the lawless.

title: Cling to the holy and stop tearing Christ's body
english: So we too must hold fast to such examples, brothers and sisters.
For it is written: “Join yourselves to the holy ones, because those who join themselves to them will be made holy.”
And again in another place he says: “With an innocent man you will be innocent, and with one of the elect you will be elect, and with a crooked one you will be perverted.”
Let us be joined, then, to the innocent and the righteous, and these are the elect of God.
Why are there strifes and outbursts of anger and dissensions and divisions and war among you?
Do we not have one God and one Christ and one Spirit of grace poured out upon us, and one calling in Christ?
Why do we tear apart and rip apart the members of Christ, and make faction against our own body, and reach such madness that we forget that we are members of one another?
Remember the words of the Lord Jesus.

For he said: “Woe to that man! It would have been good for him if he had not been born, than to cause one of my elect to stumble. It would be better for him to have a millstone hung around his neck and be drowned in the sea, than to pervert one of my elect.”
Your division has perverted many, thrown many into despair, many into doubt, all of us into grief, and your faction persists.
orientation: The Roman church has just finished praising those who endured under envy, and now turns directly to the Corinthians with a command to join themselves to the holy and a rebuke for their divisions.

title: The Corinthians' Faction Shames Their Ancient Church
english: Take up the letter of the blessed apostle Paul. What did he write to you first, at the beginning of the gospel? He wrote to you in truth and in the Spirit about himself and Cephas and Apollos, because even then you had formed partialities. But that partiality brought you a lesser sin, for you leaned toward apostles who had been witnessed to and toward a man approved by them.

Now consider who has twisted you and diminished the solemn dignity of your renowned love of the brethren. It is shameful, beloved, exceedingly shameful, and unworthy of your conduct in Christ, to hear that the most steadfast and ancient church of the Corinthians is making faction against the elders because of one or two individuals. And this report has reached not only us but also those who are differently inclined from us, so that blasphemies are brought upon the name of the Lord because of your foolishness, and you bring danger upon yourselves.
orientation: The Roman church, having just lamented the Corinthians' persistent faction, now turns to the example of the apostle Paul's letter and the shame their division has brought on the church's ancient reputation.

title: The Gate of Righteousness and the Call to Humility
english: So let us remove this quickly and fall before the Lord. Let us weep and beg him to be merciful and be reconciled to us, and to restore us to the pure and reverent conduct of our love for one another.
For this is the gate of righteousness opened to life, as it is written: “Open to me the gates of righteousness, so that I may enter through them and confess to the Lord” (Psalm 118:19).
“This is the gate of the Lord; the righteous shall enter through it” (Psalm 118:20).

Many gates are open, but this one in righteousness is the one in Christ. Blessed are all who enter through it and direct their journey in holiness and righteousness, accomplishing everything without disturbance.
Let someone be faithful. Let someone be able to speak knowledge. Let someone be wise in discerning words. Let someone be pure in deeds.
For the more someone seems to be greater, the more he ought to be humble, and to seek what benefits everyone, not what benefits himself.
orientation: The Roman church is urging the Corinthians to end their faction quickly by turning to God in repentance, and now grounds this appeal in the image of the open gate of righteousness from Psalm 117 LXX.

title: The Bond of Love in Christ
english: Let the one who has love in Christ do what Christ commands.
Who can explain the bond of God's love?
Who is able to tell the greatness of its beauty?
The height to which love leads is beyond telling.

Love glues us to God. Love covers a multitude of sins (1 Peter 4:8). Love endures all things, is patient with all things (1 Corinthians 13:7). There is nothing vulgar in love, nothing arrogant. Love has no division. Love does not make faction. Love does everything in harmony. In love all the elect of God were perfected. Without love nothing is pleasing to God.
In love the Master received us. Because of the love he had for us, Jesus Christ our Lord gave his blood for us by the will of God, and his flesh for our flesh, and his soul for our souls.
orientation: The Roman church is exhorting the Corinthians to pursue love, which it presents as the bond that unites believers to God and perfects the elect.

title: Love's perfection and the blessedness of the forgiven
english: You see, beloved, how great and wonderful love is. Its perfection is beyond all explanation. Who is able to be found in it, except those whom God deems worthy? Let us ask and plead from his mercy, then, that we may be found in love without human partiality, blameless.

All the generations from Adam until this day have passed away. But those who were perfected in love according to the grace of God hold a place among the pious. They will be made manifest at the visitation of the kingdom of Christ. For it is written: "Enter the chambers for a little while, until my anger and wrath pass by" (Isaiah 26:20), "and I will remember a good day and raise you up from your tombs."

We are blessed, beloved, if we do the commandments of God in the harmony of love, so that our sins may be forgiven us through love. For it is written: "Blessed are those whose lawless deeds are forgiven and whose sins are covered; blessed is the man whose sin the Lord will not count, and in whose mouth there is no deceit" (Psalm 32:1-2).
This blessing came upon the elect of God through Jesus Christ our Lord, to whom be glory forever and ever. Amen.
orientation: Clement has just praised love at length and now turns to the greatness of love, the need to be found in it without human partiality, and the blessedness of those whose sins are forgiven through love.

title: Confession versus hardening, with the examples of Korah and Pharaoh
english: So then, for whatever we fell aside in and did because of certain intrusions of the adversary, let us ask that it be forgiven us. And those who became leaders of faction and division also owe it to consider the common hope.

For those who conduct themselves with fear and love would rather fall into mistreatments themselves than have their neighbors do so. Rather, they bring condemnation on themselves than on the harmony that was handed down to us so well and justly.

For it is good for a person to confess his transgressions rather than to harden his heart, just as the heart of those who made faction against Moses, the servant of God, was hardened. Their judgment became clear:
for they went down into Hades alive, and death will shepherd them.

Pharaoh and his army and all the leaders of Egypt, their chariots and their riders, were sunk into the Red Sea and perished for no other reason than this: their foolish hearts were hardened after the signs and wonders had happened in the land of Egypt through Moses, the servant of God.
orientation: The author, writing from the church in Rome to the Corinthians, has just spoken of the blessing of forgiven sins and now turns to the need for confession and the fate of those who harden their hearts in faction.

title: God needs nothing but confession
english: Brothers and sisters, the Master of all things lacks nothing. He needs nothing from anyone except one thing: that they confess to him.
For David, one of the elect, says: “I will confess to the Lord, and it will please him more than a young calf that grows horns and hooves. Let the poor see it and be glad.”
And again he says: “Sacrifice to God a sacrifice of praise, and pay your vows to the Most High. Call on me in the day of your trouble, and I will rescue you, and you will glorify me.”
For the sacrifice to God is a broken spirit.
orientation: The Roman church is addressing the Corinthians, urging them away from faction by showing that what God truly wants from people is not sacrifice but confession, praise, and a broken spirit.

title: Moses intercedes for Israel after the golden calf
english: You know the sacred writings well, dear friends, and you have bent over the oracles of God. So I am writing these things to remind you.

When Moses went up the mountain and spent forty days and forty nights in fasting and humility, God said to him: “Go down from here quickly, because your people, whom you led out of the land of Egypt, have broken the law. They have quickly turned aside from the way you commanded them, and they have made molten images for themselves.”

And the Lord said to him: “I have spoken to you once and twice, saying: I have seen this people, and look, they are stiff-necked. Let me destroy them, and I will wipe out their name from under heaven, and I will make you into a great and wonderful nation, far more numerous than this one.”
But Moses said: “By no means, Lord. Forgive the sin of this people, or else wipe me out of the book of the living.”
What great love! What unsurpassable perfection! A servant speaks boldly to the Lord, asks forgiveness for the multitude, or even asks to be wiped out along with them.
orientation: The Roman church is writing to the Corinthians, reminding them of Scripture examples of intercession and self-sacrifice, and now turns to Moses pleading for Israel after the golden calf.

title: Whoever loves peace should withdraw for the flock's sake
english: So who among you is noble? Who is tender-hearted? Who is filled with love? Let that person speak: “If faction and strife and divisions have come about because of me, I will withdraw. I will leave, wherever you wish, and I will do what the multitude commands. Only let the flock of Christ be at peace with the appointed elders.”
Whoever does this will win great glory for himself in Christ, and every place will receive him, for “the earth is the Lord’s and everything in it” (Psalm 24:1).
Those who live as citizens of God’s commonwealth that brings no regret have done these things and will do them.
orientation: Clement, writing from the Roman church to the Corinthian church, has just praised Moses' self-sacrificing intercession and now turns to address directly anyone in Corinth who is noble, compassionate, and full of love.

title: Gentile examples of self-giving love
english: Let us also bring forward examples from the nations. Many kings and rulers, when a time of plague had set in, received an oracle and handed themselves over to death, so that through their own blood they might rescue their citizens. Many withdrew from their own cities, so that they might no longer be in faction.
We know many among us who handed themselves over to chains, so that they might ransom others. Many handed themselves over to slavery, and taking the price paid for them, they fed others.
Many women, strengthened through the grace of God, accomplished many courageous deeds.
Blessed Judith, when the city was under siege, asked the elders to allow her to go out to the camp of the foreigners.
So she handed herself over to danger and went out, for love of her homeland and of the people who were under siege, and the Lord delivered Holofernes into the hand of a woman.

No less did Esther, perfect in faith, put herself in danger, so that she might rescue the nation of Israel that was about to perish. For through her fasting and her humility she entreated the All-Seeing Master of the ages, who saw the lowliness of her soul and rescued the people for whose sake she had faced danger.
orientation: Clement is still urging the Corinthians to imitate those who sacrifice themselves for the community, now turning to examples from the nations and from Jewish women.

title: Accepting God's discipline
english: So let us intercede for those who are caught in some transgression, asking that gentleness and humility be given to them, so that they may yield not to us but to the will of God. For in this way their remembrance before God and the saints will be fruitful and complete, accompanied by compassion.
Let us take up discipline, beloved, at which no one should be offended. The admonition we offer one another is good and exceedingly beneficial, for it binds us to the will of God.
For the holy word says: “The Lord disciplined me with discipline, and he did not hand me over to death. For the Lord disciplines the one he loves, and he whips every son whom he receives.”
“A righteous man will discipline me in mercy,” it says, “and will reprove me, but let not the oil of sinners anoint my head.”

And again it says: “Blessed is the man whom the Lord reproves; do not reject the admonition of the Almighty. For he causes pain, and again he restores; he struck, and his hands healed. Six times he will deliver you from troubles, and in the seventh no evil will touch you. In famine he will rescue you from death, and in war he will release you from the hand of iron. He will hide you from the whip of the tongue, and you will not fear evils when they come. You will laugh at the unrighteous and the lawless, and you will not fear wild beasts; for wild beasts will be at peace with you. Then you will know that your house will be at peace, and the conduct of your tent will not fail. You will know that your offspring is many, and your children like the abundant grass of the field. You will come to the grave like ripe wheat harvested in season, or like a heap on the threshing floor gathered in at the right time.”
You see, beloved, how great is the protection for those who are disciplined by the Master. For being a good Father, he disciplines us so that we may receive mercy through his holy discipline.
orientation: The author, writing from the church in Rome, urges the Corinthians to intercede for those caught in wrongdoing and to accept God's corrective discipline as a sign of his fatherly love.

title: Warning to the Faction-Makers: Submit or Perish
english: So then, you who laid the foundation of this faction: submit to the elders, and accept discipline that leads you into repentance. Bend the knees of your heart.

Learn to submit. Put off the boastful and proud self-will of your tongue, because it is better for you to be found small and reputable in the flock of Christ than to appear great through preeminence and be cast out from his hope.
For this is what the all-virtuous Wisdom says: "Look, I will pour out to you the utterance of my breath, and I will teach you my word" (Proverbs 1:23).

"Because I called and you would not obey, I stretched out my words and you paid no attention" (Proverbs 1:24). "You made my counsels void and disobeyed my reproofs. So I in turn will laugh at your destruction, and I will gloat when ruin comes upon you, when sudden tumult arrives, when catastrophe overtakes you like a storm, when affliction and siege come upon you."

"Then you will call upon me, but I will not listen to you. Evil people will seek me and will not find me, because they hated wisdom and did not choose the fear of the Lord" (Proverbs 1:28-29). "They had no wish to attend to my counsels, and they mocked my reproofs."
"Therefore they will eat the fruits of their own way, and they will be filled with their own impiety."

"For the wrongs they did to the innocent, they will be slain, and searching judgment will destroy the impious. But the one who listens to me will dwell in hope, trusting, and will be quiet, with no fear of any evil" (Proverbs 1:32-33).
orientation: The Roman church, having just quoted Job on God's fatherly discipline, now turns directly to the Corinthians who started the faction and commands them to submit to the elders and repent, quoting Wisdom's warning to the disobedient.

title: Obedience to God's holy name and the reward of the saved
english: Let us obey His all-holy and glorious name, then, and flee from the threats that Wisdom spoke beforehand against the disobedient. Then we may dwell in trust upon the most holy name of His majesty.

Accept our counsel, and you will have no regret. For as God lives, and as the Lord Jesus Christ lives, and as the Holy Spirit lives, and as the faith and hope of the elect live, so surely the one who has done the righteous acts and commandments given by God, in humility with earnest gentleness, without regret, will be enrolled and counted among the number of those being saved through Jesus Christ. Through Him is the glory to God unto the ages of the ages. Amen.
orientation: The Roman church is concluding its appeal to the Corinthians, urging them to obey God and accept the letter's counsel so that they may be counted among the saved.

title: Warning to the disobedient and prayer for preservation
english: But if any disobey what he has said through us, let them know that they will bind themselves in transgression and no small danger.

We, however, will be innocent of this sin. We will ask with earnest prayer and supplication that the creator of all things may keep unbroken, through his beloved child Jesus Christ, the number that has been counted of his elect throughout the whole world. Through him he called us from darkness to light, from ignorance to the knowledge of the glory of his name.

We ask that we may hope in your name, the name that is the beginning of all creation. You have opened the eyes of our heart to know you, the only highest in the highest, holy, resting among the holy. You humble the pride of the arrogant; you dissolve the plans of nations; you make the lowly high and bring the high low; you make rich and make poor; you kill and make alive. You alone are the finder of spirits and God of all flesh, watching over the deeps, the overseer of human works, the helper of those in danger, the savior of the despairing, the creator and bishop of every spirit. You multiply nations on the earth, and from all of them you have chosen those who love you through Jesus Christ, your beloved child, through whom you have trained us, sanctified us, honored us.

We ask you, Master, to be our helper and protector. Save those among us who are in affliction; have mercy on the lowly; raise the fallen; appear to those in need; heal the sick; turn back the wandering among your people; feed the hungry; ransom our prisoners; lift up the weak; comfort the fainthearted. Let all the nations know you, that you alone are God, and Jesus Christ is your child, and we are your people and the sheep of your pasture.
orientation: Clement has just finished urging obedience and is now warning those who disobey what has been said through him, before turning to a long prayer to God.

title: Prayer for cleansing, guidance, and peace
english: You have made the enduring order of the world visible through the things that are at work in it. You, Lord, created the inhabited earth. You are faithful in every generation, just in your judgments, wonderful in strength and majesty, wise in creating and understanding in establishing what has come to be, good in what is seen and kind to those who trust in you, merciful and compassionate. Forgive our lawless deeds, our injustices, our transgressions, and our offenses.
